tools.name: create_key
tools.description: Create a random PUBLIC key, absolute TTL (default one hour). No credentials returned; anyone knowing the ID can modify it.

tools.name: get_key
tools.description: Read exact string value, metadata and ETag. May renew sliding TTL with write access; refuses burn values.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: Inspect metadata and ETag without reading values, renewing expiry or consuming burn keys.

tools.name: put_key
tools.description: Create or replace UTF-8 text. Existing protection remains; absolute deadlines cannot extend. Preconditions prevent lost updates.

tools.name: patch_key
tools.description: Apply JSON Merge Patch text with an exact quoted ETag. Null members delete; arrays/scalars replace. No blind retries.

tools.name: delete_key
tools.description: Permanently delete a key with write access and optional ETag. Missing keys return 404.

tools.name: touch_key
tools.description: Renew TTL with write access, within the existing absolute deadline. Never revive expired keys.

tools.name: increment_counter
tools.description: Atomically increment a signed 64-bit counter; optional clamps and bounded history. Never retry blindly.

tools.name: decrement_counter
tools.description: Atomically decrement a signed 64-bit counter; optional clamps and bounded history. Never retry blindly.

tools.name: get_counter_history
tools.description: Read opted-in UTC history: 168 hourly, 90 daily or 24 monthly buckets; ISO start inclusive/end exclusive.

tools.name: wait_for_change
tools.description: Wait up to 30 seconds for a visible change. Timeout is normal; no replay or burn values. Maximum two concurrent waits/IP.

tools.name: find_tools
tools.description: Search the catalog of free utility tools by what you want to do, e.g. "csv to json" or "sha256". Returns slugs for describe_tool and run_tool.

tools.name: describe_tool
tools.description: Get one utility tool's input schema, defaults and worked examples before running it.

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description:
Run a utility tool with its named inputs. On error, message, fix and problems say which input to change.
Text tools answer at once and store nothing. File tools (tier "job") take file references from the drop tool
and answer with result and files, or, if still running after wait_seconds (default 10)

semaphore
tools.description:
Counting semaphore: at most `limit` concurrent holders, each with an owner_token and fence. Same actions
as lease. Use it to cap how many agents work in parallel.

seq; entries(after=cursor) returns entries and next; wait_seconds (up to 30) waits for new entries. Oldest
entries are dropped at the size limit (truncated true).

tools.name: wait_for_any
tools.description:
Wait up to 30 seconds for the first change among 1–10 targets: {"key": k, "etag": optional} or
{"object": id, "version": optional int}. Returns changed targets (deletion counts), or status timeout.
All targets use the configured credential. Burn keys are refused.

tools.name: rate_limit
tools.description:
Shared token bucket so several agents can split one quota (for example an external API's). take(tokens,
default 1) returns granted true with remaining, or granted false with retry_after_ms. Never blocks.

Dead-man switch for a person or a long job: unless someone checks in every interval_seconds (60+, default

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: mailbox, drop, job, file_request, form, poll, status_page, relay · Private data: create_key, run_tool, lease, capture, mailbox, wait_for_any, rate_limit, approval, secret, drop, job, pipeline, deadman, file_request, form, status_page, relay · Public sink: capture, mailbox, heartbeat, secret, drop, schedule, form, poll, status_page · Destructive: create_key, patch_key, delete_key, run_tool, drop, pipeline, schedule, file_request, form, status_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: mailbox, drop, job, file_request, form, poll, status_page, relay · Private data: create_key, run_tool, lease, capture, mailbox, wait_for_any, rate_limit, approval, secret, drop, job, pipeline, deadman, file_request, form, status_page, relay · Public sink: capture, mailbox, heartbeat, secret, drop, schedule, form, poll, status_page · Destructive: create_key, patch_key, delete_key, run_tool, drop, pipeline, schedule, file_request, form, status_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
